prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1266; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at an intersection. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the scene photographs. Responding officers and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the collision happened as described.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account consistent with the claimant's. The damage to the claimant's vehicle lines up with the angle and force of the impact shown in the photos.

Entry 4: Medical records show a shoulder injury of a kind typical for a force like this crash. Earlier records also reflect a minor strain in the same area years ago that healed fully with no lasting effects.

Entry 5: Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy tapering as the claimant's range of motion improved. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle had prior damage, and no damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 6: The claimant has given the same account of the accident in each conversation, including the recorded statement taken through counsel. Coverage was confirmed and the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 7: Based on the records reviewed, the injury, vehicle damage, and reported sequence of events are consistent with one another. File moved to the bodily injury evaluation queue for counsel's demand package.
